The chapter also presents a 44-group 1985 counterpart derived from balanced 1998, with reconstructed early catches. Stored 28_726_Guinea_(1985) is the distinct 35-group, 42,969 km² shelf revision in the 2009 report. Hash-suffixed copies are extraction identities, not extra baselines.   Stored 1985 identity

Accepted canonical parameters retained. Native database JSON differs only in 44 added taxonomy descriptions. Table 9 (p.143/PDF 147) has 13 B/EE values outside strict printed-rounding bounds; PB/QB agree at displayed precision. Oiseaux TL 3.77 differs from accepted calculated 3.545. Coarse diets and reconstructed catch/discards remain limitations. Inherited diet normalization changes cells by at most 3.07×10⁻⁸; default GS, derived BA and import 45 remain accepted conventions. Deep-water fish are weak predatory, habitat or family analogues of the source Gempylus, Lepidocybium or other bathy members. Exact placement and size/depth boundaries remain unverified; mixed diets and pelagic overlap weaken the pooled pathway. Lampris also has an uncertain local role.

Barrelfishes and armoured gurnards are weak benthopelagic-feeder analogues of source Ariomma or Trigla. Heterogeneous diets, uncertain local feeding and shelf/slope overlap leave source-specific placement unresolved.
The shelf croaker has a weak source medium-predator habitat connection, supported by 80–200 m occurrence and fish/shrimp feeding. Exact membership and pooled diet fit remain uncertain.
